;Business and economy
*[[Japan]] launches a [[Japanese yen|¥]]70 billion payment scheme to pay firms to move factories out of [[China]] to either Japan itself or countries within the [[Southeast Asia]]n region in an attempt to better secure its [[supply chain]]s. 57 firms, including face mask manufacturer [[Iris Ohyama]], are among the first to receive the subsidy. [https://www.bloombergquint.com/global-economics/japan-to-pay-at-least-536-million-for-companies-to-leave-china (Bloomberg)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Crime in France]]
**A fire inside [[Nantes Cathedral]] in [[Nantes]], [[France]], destroys the 400-year-old grand organ, which had survived two major fires in [[1944]] and [[1972]], and some [[stained glass window]]s. [[law enforcement in France|Police]] are treating the fire as [[arson]], saying three fires appear to have been started deliberately. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53455142 (BBC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****[[New York (State)|New York]] records 743 hospitalizations, its lowest since March 18. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/new-york-coronavirus-hospitalizations-fall/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Texas]]
****Around 85 infants in [[Nueces County, Texas|Nueces County]] test positive for coronavirus. [https://thehill.com/blogs/blog-briefing-room/news/507958-85-infants-test-positive-for-covid-19-in-texas-county-amid (''The Hill'')]
***The [[Food and Drug Administration]] issues an emergency use authorization for COVID-19 pool [[COVID-19 testing|testing]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/18/health/pool-testing-fda-authorization/index.html (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[President of Iran|President]] [[Hassan Rouhani]] says that the health ministry estimated as many as 25 million [[Iranian peoples|Iranians]] have been infected by the virus and that 30 to 35 million will be infected in the coming months as he urges the public to take the virus seriously. [https://apnews.com/259e21771a0dcc0551e101bfe945bdb4 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] becomes the country with most cases in [[Southeast Asia]], recording 84,882 infections, while authorities say that the actual number could be much higher due to undetected cases. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-indonesia/indonesia-overtakes-china-with-highest-coronavirus-cases-in-east-asia-idUSKCN24J0DY?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***Victoria Premier [[Daniel Andrews]] announces that [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|masks]] will be mandatory in the [[Melbourne]] area. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-07-19/victoria-coronavirus-cases-climb-masks-become-mandatory/12470424 (ABC Net AU)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
***[[Romania]] surpasses 2,000 deaths from COVID-19 and sets a daily record of 889 new cases. [https://www.romania-insider.com/coronavirus-cases-romania-july-17-2020 (Romania Insider)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[List of George Floyd protests in the United States|George Floyd protests in the United States]]
***[[George Floyd protests in Illinois]]
****[[George Floyd protests in Chicago]]
*****Protesters gather near the home of [[Mayor of Chicago|Chicago Mayor]] [[Lori Lightfoot]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/19/us/chicago-protest-lori-lightfoot/index.html (CNN)]
***[[George Floyd protests in Oregon]]
****[[George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon|George Floyd protests in Portland]]
*****Several protesters in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]], [[Oregon]], are arrested. Authorities said protesters allegedly blocked exits of government buildings and launched fireworks. Saturday morning's arrests came after the [[Billy J. Williams| US Attorney for Oregon]] on Friday requested an investigation into masked, camouflaged federal authorities who have recently arrested Portland protesters. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/18/us/portland-protest-arrests/index.html (CNN)]
**[[List of George Floyd protests outside the United States]]
***[[George Floyd protests in Canada]]
****Three [[Black Lives Matter]] protesters are charged in [[Toronto]] for pouring pink paint on the statues of [[John A. Macdonald]] at [[Queen's Park (Toronto)|Queen's Park]] and [[Egerton Ryerson]] at [[Ryerson University]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/amp/1.5654829 (CBC News)]
***[[Human rights in France#Police abuses and detention conditions|Policy brutality in France]]
****Protesters mark the anniversary of the death of [[Death of Adama Traoré| Adama Traoré]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jul/18/paris-protesters-mark-fourth-anniversary-of-adama-traore-death (''The Guardian'')] 
*Aftermath of the [[Sudanese Revolution]], [[Late-2019 Sudanese protests]]
**The [[Government of Sudan|government]] announces legal action against activists and journalists who "insulted" the [[Sudanese Armed Forces|military]]. They had accused the military of various killings during last year's protests, which the army denies. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sudan-politics/sudans-army-launches-legal-action-against-insulting-activists-idUSKCN24J0N7?il=0 (Reuters)]
**Amid a reform of the country's Islamist laws, [[Sudan]] lifts the [[Capital punishment in Sudan|death penalty]] for homosexuality and ends flogging as punishment for [[LGBT rights in Sudan|homosexuals]]. [https://africa.cgtn.com/2020/07/17/great-first-step-as-sudan-lifts-death-penalty-and-flogging-for-homosexuality/ (CGTN)]
*Seven people aged between 17 to 22 are found dead, some with gunshot wounds, near [[Gatun Lake]] in [[Panama]]. The group are believed to have gone out to swim on the lake when the attack took place. The motive for the attack is also under investigation. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/panama-youths-killed-brutal-attack-lake-200719005743322.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
*****The [[2020 Thai protests|largest street demonstration]] in [[Thailand]] since the [[2014 Thai coup d'état]] erupts at the [[Democracy Monument]] in [[Bangkok]] with around 2,500 protesters demanding the government's resignation, parliament's dissolution, and the rewriting of the constitution, defying a coronavirus ban on gatherings [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-thailand-protests/thai-protesters-call-for-government-to-resign-idUSKCN24J0HN (Reuters)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
*****[[Israelis]] protest [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] for his handling of COVID-19 and corruption. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-israel-protests-idUSKCN24J0TH (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] delays [[Parliament of Australia|parliament]] due to the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-australia-idUSKCN24J01V (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Russian protests]]
**About 50,000 people take part in a second Saturday protest rally in [[Khabarovsk]], [[Russia]], against the arrest of Governor [[Sergei Furgal]] on charges of involvement in multiple murders 15 years ago, which Furgal denies. The protests, which also reflect the  simmering discontent with the [[Government of Russia|Kremlin’s]] policies, are the largest ever in Khabarovsk, a city of 590,000. The police didn't interfere with the rally. Protests are also taking place in [[Vladivostok]] and [[Komsomolsk-on-Amur]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/av/world-europe-53455954/sergei-furgal-fresh-protests-in-khabarovsk-over-governor-s-arrest (BBC News)] [https://www.euronews.com/2020/07/18/massive-protests-in-russia-after-arrest-of-people-s-governor-sergei-furgal (EuroNews)]
*[[Kuwait]]'s 91-year-old [[Emir of Kuwait|Emir]], [[Sabah Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah]], is  admitted to hospital for what aides described as  "routine" medical tests.  [[Crown Prince]] [[Nawaf Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah]], the Emir's 83-year-old half-brother and designated successor, will temporarily carry out some of the Emir's duties. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53459994 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/kuwait-sheikh-sabah-admitted-hospital-medical-checks-200718143551522.html (Al Jazeera)]
